title: Slide a handheld mic into its clip on a light desk stand, holding the stand, and aim it at a marked spot
instruction: Turn the stand's clip toward the red circle. Holding the stand, slide the mic tail first into the clip until snug, then let go.
context: Teachers, panel hosts, podcasters and church volunteers put a handheld mic in the clip on a desk stand and turn it toward whoever will speak. The Shure A25D clip that comes with the SM58 grips the mic's tapered handle in sprung plastic jaws: the tail end goes into the clip and the mic is pushed back until the taper wedges snug. A light tripod desk stand such as the 363 g On-Stage DS7425 slides or tips over under that push, so people hold the stand with one hand and push the mic in with the other. To aim it, the stand is lifted a little and turned so the clip points at the speaker's place, marked here by a red circle on the table. The robot has to turn the stand, hold it, line the mic's tail up with the clip's open end, slide the mic in until snug without knocking the stand over, and let go with the mic pointing at the circle.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. 1) Stand: an On-Stage DS7425 tripod desktop mic stand (published: height 4.3-6.7 in, 7.5 in tripod base, rubber feet; listed weight 12.8 oz, 363 g), set to 152 (6.0 in) from the table to the top of its 5/8 in-27 thread, its tube's centre on a taped cross at (165, 0). Its own tapered clip is not used. 2) Clip: the Shure A25D supplied with the SM58 (published: fits 25-30 mm barrels, swivels through 180 degrees), screwed tight on the stand's thread, its swivel's thumb nut tightened with the clip level (phone level along it). The stand starts turned so the clip's front end points 20 degrees to the robot's right of straight ahead (heading -20 degrees; mark it with a taped line under one leg). 3) Mic: a Shure SM58 (published: 162 long, grille 51 across, handle 23 across at the tail, 298 g), lying on the table on its grille and tail end, grille toward the robot's right (along -y), tail end's centre at (210, -108). 4) Red circle: a 60 mm red paper disc taped flat on the table, centre at (315, -260), 300 from the stand's cross at heading -60 degrees. Estimates (check with a ruler, a kitchen scale and a phone level): A25D bore 25.4 across at rest, 36 long, opening at the top 21.5 wide, swivel axis 20 above the thread's top, mic axis 41 above it, front end slightly flared; SM58 handle 26.4 across at 60 from the tail and 34 at 112; stand tube 19 across up to a 28 mm clutch at 125-139, hub 34 across, feet on a 180 circle. Push needed to slide the mic in snug: about 4-6 N (stand the clip upright on a kitchen scale and push the mic in tail first; the reading rises by the push). Frictions: rubber feet 0.8, clip plastic 0.35, mic paint 0.4. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every collider, joint and mass.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from the top-camera video, a top photo, a side photo and a ruler (in simulation from the poses). Score 0 if the stand tipped over at any time (its tube more than 20 degrees from upright), if the mic is not held in the clip (its handle is not inside the clip's jaws, it touches the table, or it fell off), if a gripper is still within 3 cm of the mic or the stand's tube, or if the mic moved more than 1 mm in its last second. Otherwise the score is the lowest of these four numbers. Seat: 1.0 if at least 8 mm of handle sticks out behind the clip's back face (the taper is wedged snug), else 0.5. Aim, on the top photo: extend the mic's axis from its tail end through the grille's centre and measure the shortest distance from the red circle's centre to that line, on the grille side: 1.0 up to 30 mm, 0.75 over 30 up to 60 mm, 0.5 over 60 up to 100 mm, 0.25 over 100 mm. Stand: its tube's centre within 20 mm of the taped cross 1.0, over 20 up to 50 mm 0.75, over 50 mm 0.5. Tilt, on the side photo: the mic's axis within 12 degrees of level 1.0, otherwise 0.5. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: About 1 minute. Holding the stand, pull the mic out of the clip toward its grille and lay it back at its start spot on its grille and tail end, grille toward the robot's right. Stand the stand back on its taped cross turned to heading -20 degrees (the taped line under its leg), and check the clip is still level (phone level along it); retighten the thumb nut if the swivel moved. The A25D's jaws loosen with use: if the mic slides out of the clip under its own weight with the grille tipped down once 8 mm of handle sticks out, fit a new A25D. Return both arms to the ready pose.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The clip's flexing plastic C is two hinged jaws on a stiff spring with a small preload (estimated so the slide-in takes about 4-6 N, under the arm's limits); the swivel is tight, so the clip is fixed level; the height clutch holds by joint friction (40 N, estimate). The mic's handle is two straight tapers and its grille a ball, of uniform density. Clip, tube, leg and taper sizes, frictions and the stand's weight split are estimates; the clip's front 6 mm is a flared lead-in.
